name: Ticket Tailor
shortDescription: A UK-founded event ticketing platform for paid and free events, with website embedding, attendee management and published per-ticket fees.
suitableContexts: Churches running paid or free events
Teams that want control of ticketing on their own website

pricing.summary: Ticket Tailor publishes UK pricing from £0.22 plus VAT per paid ticket when credits are bought in advance, or £0.60 plus VAT pay-as-you-go. Payment-provider fees are separate; it also publishes a 50% discount on its fees for eligible charities.

editorial.assessment: Ticket Tailor is a strong UK comparison candidate for churches running events because it publishes GBP per-ticket pricing, offers a stated charity discount and lets a church choose a payment provider. The real comparison must include VAT, processor fees, refund policy and the public booking experience.
bestFor: Churches selling tickets or taking registrations for events and courses
Teams wanting booking pages embedded on a church website
strengths: Published charity discount on Ticket Tailor fees
Payment provider is separated from the ticketing platform
limitations: Gift Aid workflows and charity-discount eligibility must be confirmed

procurementVerdict.problem: Churches selling tickets or taking registrations for events and courses

longForm.verdict: Ticket Tailor is a particularly useful UK option when event registration is becoming an administrative burden but the church still wants the event journey to feel like its own. Its fee model is intelligible, but the cost that matters is the complete checkout: platform fee, VAT, processor fee and refund handling.

decisionLens.heading: The ticket price is only one part of the promise to an attendee.
decisionLens.text: A paid event creates an expectation of a clear confirmation, accessible booking experience and straightforward support if plans change. Trial the attendee journey, not simply the staff dashboard, and decide in advance who owns cancellations and refunds.

sections.heading: Fees, payments and charity discount
sections.question: How should a church calculate the likely cost?
paragraphs: Ticket Tailor lists prepaid credits from £0.22 plus VAT per paid ticket and pay-as-you-go at £0.60 plus VAT, with payment-provider charges separate. It says eligible charities can receive 50% off its own fees.

Model a typical event and a difficult one: a free event, a paid event, a refund and a cancellation. Confirm eligibility and current fees before setting ticket prices, and do not assume the platform itself handles Gift Aid.

userFeedback.summary: This profile does not use an independent review score. It is based on Ticket Tailor’s public GBP pricing and charity-discount information.
themes: Published per-ticket fees make event-level cost modelling possible.
The payment provider remains a separate decision and cost.
userFeedback.caveat: Published fees and charity discounts can change, and a church’s VAT, processor and refund obligations depend on its own circumstances.

faq.question: How much does Ticket Tailor cost in the UK?
faq.answer: Ticket Tailor lists prepaid paid-ticket fees from £0.22 plus VAT, or £0.60 plus VAT pay-as-you-go. Payment processing costs are separate.

faq.question: Does Ticket Tailor offer charity pricing?
faq.answer: Ticket Tailor says eligible charities receive 50% off its own fees. Its help information says this does not discount the separate payment-processor fees.

faq.question: Does Ticket Tailor handle Gift Aid?
faq.answer: Gift Aid support was not confirmed in this profile. Ask the supplier and obtain appropriate charity-finance advice before designing a Gift Aid process around ticket sales.
